Re: Fw: Facebook communication
[contact omitted] Parker, Nealin Thursday, May 2, 2013 at 9:30:44 AM Eastern Daylight Time
To: [contact omitted] McSpedon, Joseph
Cc: [contact omitted] Sweet, Andrew, [contact omitted] Stephen Lennon, [contact omitted] Megan Swanson
10:30 it is! Food court or your desk?
On Thu, May 2, 2013 at 9:26 AM, McSpedon, Joseph <[contact omitted]> wrote:
I can do 10:30.
On Thu, May 2, 2013 at 9:06 AM, Parker, Nealin <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Andrew -
I can make 10:30, but copying in Joe, who is, frankly, more important. :)
Nealin
On Wed, May 1, 2013 at 9:08 PM, Sweet, Andrew <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Nealin,
Sounds very interesting. Would be great to meet up with you to hear abou this and other things. Just got back from
Colombia this am and off to Cape Town on Tuesday. Would Friday at 10:30am work? I may have some ideas on
the Fbook partnership too. Let me know if this works and hope to see you soon!
Andrew
On Wed, May 1, 2013 at 8:58 PM, Nealin Parker <[contact omitted]> wrote:
So the deal is that we have had these super interesting individual programs in partnership with facebook--
preventing violence, hate crimes, exploring organising for peace in high stakes environments. Joe explains in
more detail below, but do you think there is anyone in the FO or beyond who would be interested? It's in my
mind a great set of individual opportunities, but also an excellent relationship if we should find ourselves in
anything like another arab spring.
Hope all is well with you--do vou ever get coffee?
J. Nealin Parker
Director (Acting)
Office of Transition Initiatives
Bureau of Democracy, Conflict and Humanitarian Assistance, USAID
Ronald Reagan Building
1300 Pennsylvania Ave., NW, B3.6.124
Washington DC 20004
Office: [opaque block]
[opaque block]
From: McSpedon, Joseph [mailto:[contact omitted]]
Sent: Wednesday, May 01, 2013 03:45 PM
To: Nealin Parker <[contact omitted]>; Stephen Lennon <[contact omitted]>
Subject: Facebook communication
Facebook reached out to us after some interaction related to working with NGOs focused on using Facebook as
an advocacy tool for issues related to Syria. Robbie Harris put us in context. After initial discussions | laid out
what Facebook was offering up to the teams, and thus far three teams have taken advantage of that.

Honduras - first stage of interaction is looking at the issue of Facebook use by criminal elements, and helping the
police and others recognize how they can report these as violations of Facebook's terms of service as well as
how they can monitor these sources for information. The second stage would be to look at how Facebook is
currently used in Honduras and find ways to better understand Facebook analytics to help local partners carry
Sri Lanka - initial discussion was last week focused on the use of Facebook to spread anti-Muslim hate speech.
The Sri Lanka team has sent Facebook a list (in most egregious order) of offenders for Facebook to remove
after it is determined that the content violates their terms of use. As with Honduras, we are hoping to get to a
second stage, utilizing Facebook to create counter narratives.
Kenya - Galeeb is seeking funding for a project from the Embassy with a local partner that will promote utilizing
social media to monitor extremist speech as well as train alternative voices on social media best practices. We
have not yet gotten Facebook buy in on this, but they are quite interested.
As Nealin mentioned, this is a beneficial relationship for OTI for a number of reasons. In addition, the idea that
we could start to understand some ofthe analytics that Facebook does on users from the marketing side, for our
local partners use in advocacy campaigns, represents a big opportunity for our fruitful use of social media as a
programming tool.
J. Nealin Parker
Acting Director
Office of Transition Initiatives
Bureau for Democracy, Conflict and Humanitarian Assistance
US Agency for International Development
